title: Sub-tree nodes: a node of type tree that inherits another mode
description: planning contains tree nodes made from feature-planning; each sub-tree is copied inline and its mode's config applies only below it.

g1.title: Sub-tree nodes: a node of type tree that inherits another mode
g1.body:
Model (Vineet): a sub-tree is a tree stored inline. `planning` extends `default`; it can contain nodes of type `tree` that use `feature-planning`. The two modes are edited separately. When a tree is created, the whole template is resolved and every sub-tree is copied into the planning file, nested under its tree node.
Scope works like Python indentation: a tree node's config (statuses, kinds, fields, labels, link types) applies only to the nodes below it. Nothing from the parent config flows down (for now).

Template:
```yaml
template: 1
name: planning
nodes:
  - title: Features
    children:
      - type: tree
        mode: feature-planning
        title: "Feature: Checkout"
```
Tree JSON (one file):
```json
"s7":  {"type": "tree", "mode": "feature-planning", "config": {...resolved...}, "title": "Feature: Checkout", "parent": "q3"},
"q8":  {"type": "question", "kind": "why", "title": "Why build this?", "parent": "s7"}
```
The only difference from a tree file is where it lives: a tree node holds the `mode` + resolved `config` that a tree file holds at top level. Everything else (ids, activity, revision) is the host file's.

q2.title: Why build this, and why now?
q2.body: A plan holds several features, and each feature should be planned with the same feature-planning questions and vocabulary, while the plan level keeps its own (lean) vocabulary. Copy-pasting questions, or forcing one merged config on the whole plan, does neither.

history.from:
- What problem does it solve, and what evidence shows it is real (tickets, data, requests)?
- What happens if we do nothing, or do it next quarter?
- Is this the root problem, or a symptom of something cheaper to fix?
history.to: A plan holds several features, and each feature should be planned with the same feature-planning questions and vocabulary, while the plan level keeps its own (lean) vocabulary. Copy-pasting questions, or forcing one merged config on the whole plan, does neither.

q3.title: Who uses it, and who has a stake in it?
q3.body: Mode authors composing modes; agents creating a plan and adding a sub-tree per feature (`dtree add -t tree --mode feature-planning`); humans reviewing the whole plan on one page.

history.from:
- Which user segments or roles are affected, and how many?
- Who owns the decision, who reviews it, who supports it after launch?
- Which other teams or services depend on the parts we touch?
history.to: Mode authors composing modes; agents creating a plan and adding a sub-tree per feature (`dtree add -t tree --mode feature-planning`); humans reviewing the whole plan on one page.

q4.title: What is in scope, and what is explicitly out?
q4.body:
In: node type `tree` with `mode:` in templates and at runtime; recursive resolution at tree creation (a sub-mode can itself contain tree nodes; cycle + depth 8 checks); config scoped to the tree node's descendants; CLI/API/viewer use the config of the node's scope; mode editor shows tree nodes collapsed (title + mode badge + "edit feature-planning" link), never the sub-mode's nodes.
Out (for now): parent config flowing into sub-trees; syncing existing sub-trees when the sub-mode is edited later (copies, like trees today); sub-trees in separate files.

q5.title: What does success look like, and how is it measured?
q5.body:
1) `dtree new --mode planning` gives one file where questions under each feature use feature-planning's statuses/kinds and plan-level nodes use planning's.
2) `dtree review` checks each scope against its own required kinds.
3) Existing trees, modes and all tests unchanged.
4) Mechanical change: `treeConfig(tree)` becomes `configAt(tree, nodeId)` at ~15 call sites; no new branches in core.

q7.title: What data model and API changes are needed?
q7.body:
Node: `type: "tree"` (id prefix `s`), `mode`, `config` (resolved copy, written once at creation). Tree files are untouched; the file root behaves like an implicit tree node (tree.config).
Scope: the tree node itself follows its parent's config; its descendants follow its own.
Template node: `type: tree` + `mode:`; optional `children:` replace the mode's seed nodes.
Runtime: `dtree add T -p <node> -t tree --mode feature-planning --title "Feature: X"` = resolve the mode, add the tree node, seed its nodes under it. API: `POST .../nodes` with `type: "tree", mode`.
Links: type checked in the source node's scope; no other rule.
Export/save as template: tree nodes are written as `type: tree`, `mode`, and their current children.

q8.title: Where does it live in the codebase and architecture?
q8.body:
config/scope.cjs (new): `configAt(tree, nid)`, `scopeRoot(tree, nid)`.
core/tree.cjs, choose, comments, api, cli: swap `treeConfig(tree)` -> `configAt(tree, <node>)`.
templates/apply.cjs: extract `applyNodes(tree, nodes, parent)`; a `type: tree` node resolves its mode (resolve.cjs) and recurses; cycle/depth guard next to the extends one.
templates/schema.cjs: `mode` key, `tree` type.
review/{checks,inbox,summary}: iterate per scope (root goal + each tree node).
viewer.html: `cfg()` -> `cfgAt(node)`; tree nodes get a mode badge; mode-draft view renders them collapsed.

q13.title: What are the security, privacy, and failure risks?
q13.body:
Moving a node across a scope boundary: its status/kind/fields may not exist in the new scope -> the move is refused with a clear error (re-checked by the same policies).
Cycles: a mode that contains itself, directly or via others, fails at resolve time with the chain.
Stale copies: editing feature-planning later does not change existing sub-trees (same as trees today).

history.from:
- Does it touch auth, permissions, secrets, or personal data; what is the threat model?
- What happens on partial failure, timeouts, retries, or bad input?
- Performance or cost impact at current and 10x scale?
history.to:
Moving a node across a scope boundary: its status/kind/fields may not exist in the new scope -> the move is refused with a clear error (re-checked by the same policies).
Cycles: a mode that contains itself, directly or via others, fails at resolve time with the chain.
Stale copies: editing feature-planning later does not change existing sub-trees (same as trees today).

o14.title: Scope lookup: configAt(tree, node) walks up to the nearest tree node (recommended)
o14.body: Same walk as the lock policy (`lockingNode`): nearest ancestor of type `tree` -> its `config`; none -> `tree.config` (or legacy). Every place that calls `treeConfig(tree)` today already has a node at hand, so it passes it.
pros: One function owns scoping; policies (vocab, fields, labels, roles) stay unchanged
A sub-tree behaves exactly like a tree file, so no special cases
cons: ~15 call sites in lib/ and ~7 in the viewer change from tree-level to node-level config

o15.title: Separate files per sub-tree, linked from the tree node
pros: No scoping: each file has one config
cons: Not what was asked: the plan should be one file
Cross-file refs, dangling links, two-file writes

o29.title: A tree is a tree: save type tree + mode + its current children inline
o29.body: `mode` is only the name of the template tree it came from. A template tree node with `children:` uses them instead of the mode's seeds; without children it takes the mode's seeds.
pros: One concept: a tree with sub-trees is still a tree
cons: Saved children no longer follow later edits to the sub-mode
o29.rationale: Type is still a tree; a tree with subtrees is still a tree. Mode is just an alias for a template tree.
